# izamax

> Finds the index of the element having the maximum sum of absolute values of.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import izamax from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/izamax';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
izamax( N, x, strideX ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of complex elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Input array |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | `zx` stride length |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: 0-based index of the max element, or -1 if N < 1

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
izamax.strided( N, x, strideX, offsetX ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of complex elements |
| `x` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | Complex input vector |
| ↳ `strideX` | `integer` | Stride in complex elements |
| ↳ `offsetX` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: number of elements in input vector(s)

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: 0-based index of the max element, or -1 if N < 1

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `izamax()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`IZAMAX`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/izamax.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import izamax from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/izamax';

// Index of the element with the largest |Re(x)| + |Im(x)|:
const x = new Complex128Array( [ 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, -1.0, 3.0, 4.0 ] );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = izamax( 3, x, 1 );
console.log( out ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => 2

// Using the strided interface (last two elements only):
out = izamax.strided( 2, x, 1, 1 );
console.log( out ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => 1
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `IZAMAX`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

IZAMAX finds the index of the first element having maximum \|Re(.)\| + \|Im(.)\|

### Further Details

jack dongarra, 1/15/85. modified 3/93 to return if incx .le. 0. modified 12/3/93, array(1) declarations changed to array(\*)

</section>
